institutionName: University of Natural Resources and Life Sciences, Vienna (BOKU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The spoken language in the country, the size of the city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quit easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: From a budy (another student) from the University.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I can recommend the website WG gesucht. It took time to do interviews before my stay, but I was really happy to live in a privat flat.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: A nice possibility to know people from the country.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registrered for the free spaces left only half a year before my stay. It takes time, but all my ECTS was free selected so it was quit easy process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I used the phone line to student service a lot, and that was a great help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Most of my classes I registrered to after I arrived to Vienna, because I got to know about them from other erasmus students and it was possible to registrer also during the mobility.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be open for new courses after you arrive to the host university, and don't feel stressed about the fact that the study plan is only fixed during your mobility.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was quit different from the different courses. I took some courses in german and the language made the courses difficult for me. The english courses was easier for me. For the courses in the field of studies that I already have done at UCPH the level was not too high.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Not so much contact between professor and student, and a much more professionel relationsship. Much smaller courses than I am used to from UCPH and therefor also not the same amount of work for each course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Food authencity practical course
food ingridient functionality
food supply chain management
gender, nutrition and right to food
german for science
Intensiv german refresher course
practical course in food technology
processing of plant products
soil and terroir in viticulture and oenology
technology of drinks
field trip - viticulture and oenology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
practical course in food technology was a really nice course because it was practical and teached in smaller groups with several very professionel  teachers. 
gender, nutrition and right to food was very interesting for me. It was intensiv teached over 3 weeks and gave a social-science perspective on food production.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I traveled more than I expected to cities near Vienna and on skiing trips. I can recommend buying a 'Vorteilscarde' for the trains in Austria.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I didn't use any money on books for the uni.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were 'stammtisch' one day per week where people could gather for beer after school. The overall student organisation of Vienna also offered sport activities, and then the ESN organised parties and get-together activities through out the semester.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Join the ESN organised get togethers. 
Join a sport activity from the USI, a great way to also meet austrian students. 
Join the activities in the beginning of the semester, where people are all new. Join also the whats app groups for erasmus students from BOKU.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around austria and in the neighboring countries. Fx Prague, Budapest and Slovenia. ESN held a skiing trip which was great.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: For me quit easy, maybe also because I speak german.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: USI-courses, living in a privat flat with other austrians, talk with people in your courses.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The formel relationship to the professors.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The language. the natue. the openness. the many possibilities in the city.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open to changes in your plan of courses during your mobility, and get inspired from other students courses. 
Attend one of the language courses before the semester starts that BOKU are giving. I met really nice people here, and it give you a lot to be able to talk with people in german. 
Find privat accommodation like a WG (Wohnung gemeinsam).

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I rented a bike from Swappfiets for the whole stay and also bought a semester-ticket for the public transportation.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know both austrian people in my flat and a lot of international students at the university.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Taking courses in german. 
Choosing what I wanted to do from all of the possibilities!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
